newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso votes for new parliament.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso votes for new parliament.

text.p: Burkina Faso voted for a new national assembly on Sunday with President Blaise Compaore's ruling party the only one putting up candidates nationwide and its officials confident of victory.
Witnesses reported a slow start to the poll, which was due to end at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT).
Opposition leaders, while hoping for victory, said they would be content with an increased stake in the new parliament.
"We hope that the opposition wins a majority in the national assembly," Professor Joseph Ki-Zerbo, leader of the Party for Democracy and Progress (PDP), said on the eve of polling.
"If that is not possible, we hope for a blocking minority, to propose and transform, slowly but surely towards a new Burkina Faso," he added.

The ruling Congress for Popular Democracy (CDP) held 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, which was elected in 1992 during the landlocked West African nation's return to multi-party politics.
Parliament amended the constitution in January to increase the size of the assembly to 111.
At the same time, it cleared the way for Campaore to run for a further seven year term in 1998 and further terms after that. The constitution previously limited him to one term.
Short of funds, the electoral commission borrowed ballot boxes from neighbouring Ghana for Sunday's poll. Former colonial power France sent indelible ink to ensure nobody votes twice.
A total of 13 parties contested Sunday's poll, putting up 569 candidates, 80 of them women.
Opposition parties, short of cash, have staged modest campaigns. The CDP has held more than 100 rallies in the Ouagadougou area alone during the campaign.
Opposition parties made allegations of widespread malpractice and fraud at the last election.

"We have to hope that those who last time put a lot more effort into fraud than into fair competition will be more above board this time," said Sebastian Ouedraogo, secretary general of the opposition Alliance for Democracy and Federation recently.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 military coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed.

Under pressure from Western donors for democratic reform in the early 1990s, Compaore underwent a lightning conversion to multi-party politics and was elected as the sole candidate in 1991 elections -- which opposition parties boycotted as unfair.

Burkina Faso, locked in the arid Sahel belt, exports livestock to its neighbours and increasing quantities of green beans and other fruit and vegetables to Europe. Gold mining is on the rise and plans are afoot to mine zinc and manganese.
